SCORING BASIS CHANGED — TOTALS NOW SHOWN ON THE 7-POINT CAP SCALE

All six MedCap measures are flagged Topped Out = Yes and Seven Point Cap = Yes in the CMS 2026 benchmark file. Under the cap, reaching Decile 10 (100.00% performance) earns 7 points, not 10. Deciles 1–6 are unaffected. The quality-category denominator still counts 10 points per required measure, so the realistic ceiling is 42 of 60 for five-entity reporting (Harmony: 35 of 50) — a maximum Quality score of 70%, or 21 of the 30 available CPS points.

No entity's score has fallen. The numerator is unchanged where measures sit below Decile 10; only the denominator now reflects what is actually achievable. A total previously shown as 29/60 reads as 29/42 on this scale. Target bands have been rescaled from 40/45/50-of-60 to 28/32/35-of-42 (Harmony: 23/26/29-of-35); Harmony's prior 33/37/42 bands were unreachable, since 37 and 42 both sat above its real ceiling of 35.

CMS 2026 Benchmark Thresholds — MIPS CQM

Measure Code Topped Out 7-Pt Cap Decile 1Decile 2Decile 3Decile 4Decile 5Decile 6Decile 10 Pts @ D10

Topped-Out Measures: FALL (155), CAD (6), URIN (48), DPS (134), PARK (293), and DEM (286) are all topped out — the vast majority of reporters score 100%. All six carry the 7-point cap: Decile 10 = 100.00% earns 7 points, not 10. Lower deciles map to intermediate ranges and score at face value. To maximize points, all entities must achieve 100% performance rates on each measure.

No exemption available. CMS grants alternative topped-out benchmarks — restoring the full 10 points — to a subset of measures in specialty sets with limited measure choice. The 2026 benchmark file contains 46 such rows (flagged Topped Out = Yes / Seven Point Cap = No), and they carry populated Decile 7, 8, and 9 ranges. The list is almost entirely pathology, radiology, oncology, anesthesia, and GI/QCDR measures — 143, 144, 249, 250, 317, 350, 351, 360, 364, 395–397, 405, 430, 440, 477, 489, 491, plus ACEP, CAP, GIQIC, MBHR, NHCR, QMM, RCOIR and RPAQIR registry measures. None of MedCap's six measures appear on it.

DEM (286) has a valid benchmark. The measure is scoreable — the difficulty is that its benchmark is unusually compressed: Decile 1 runs all the way to 97.20%, Decile 2 covers 97.21–99.99%, and there is nothing between that and exactly 100.00%. An entity performing at 99.7% earns 2 points; the same entity at 100.0% earns 7. DEM is effectively all-or-nothing.

Note on Topped-Out Measures: All six measures are topped out, meaning national performance rates are very high. CMS benchmarks require exactly 100% performance rate to achieve Decile 10, which under the 7-point cap is worth 7 points of the 10 in the denominator. Any patient with a missing or not-met case directly impacts your decile score. Documentation completeness is the primary driver of MIPS quality scores for MedCap Health in PY2026.

Two gates, not one. Data completeness below 75% zeroes the measure outright regardless of performance rate — and as a large practice (>15 clinicians) MedCap has no 3-point floor to fall back on. Clearing 75% completeness is the first gate; reaching 100.00% performance is the second.
